articles.title: Japanese Refiners Buy Middle East Crude Through Ship-to-Ship Transfers
articles.description: Several Japanese oil tankers are returning to the Middle East to pick up crude cargoes for Japan’s refineries, but none of these are moving into the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz. Instead, a rising number of Japan-owned or Japan-bound tankers – most of which have steered clear of the Middle East since the Iran war began – are returning to waters in the Gulf of Oman to participate in ship-to-ship (STS) transfers offshore Oman or Fujairah, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, quoting shipbrokers and tanker-tracking data. articles.title: Trump Defends Russian Diesel Deal as Energy Ceasefire Claims Unravel
articles.description: US President Donald Trump, in the face of sharp criticism from officials in Ukraine, Europe, and even his Republican party, defended his decision to allow Russian diesel exports and insisted an energy cease-fire between Kyiv and Moscow is in place despite a lack of confirmation from either side. Speaking to reporters on the White House lawn on October 12, Trump maintained that the truce was in place even as Ukrainian officials reported further Russian strikes. articles.title: Oil Carriers Linked to Japan Return to MidEast
articles.description: Oil tankers with links to Japan appear to be picking up Middle East cargoes directly in the region once again, a tentative but significant return for the first time since the war began in February that speaks to soaring freight and logistics costs.

articles.title: Super El Niño Could Ease Asia’s LNG Supply Concerns
articles.description: The super El Niño is expected to raise the winter temperatures in South Korea, Japan, and parts of China, potentially easing the gas supply needs in these key Asian LNG importers and leaving more cargoes for Europe, which struggles to fill its gas storage sites to adequate levels for this time of year. The record El Niño weather pattern in the Pacific is expected to bring warmer winter weather in Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, and parts of China, Bloomberg reports, citing major weather models for the coming winter. …

articles.title: Seadrill secures deepwater rig awards across four markets
articles.description: Offshore drilling contractor Seadrill has secured a series of contract awards and extensions for its deepwater fleet in Indonesia, Malaysia, Angola, and the US Gulf of Mexico.

articles.title: Pakistan Faces $1 Billion LNG Bill This Winter
articles.description: Pakistan will have to pay in excess of $1 billion to secure LNG supply for the winter months, as spot prices soar amid massive disruptions to Qatari term supply. The price tag will be fueled by the spot LNG prices in Asia surging to three-year highs and the plans of the Pakistani government to import 10 LNG cargoes from the spot market, at double the price at which LNG is being imported from Qatar, local daily Tribune reported on Tuesday. Amid disrupted supplies from Qatar, Pakistan will have to purchase these additional 10 cargoes on the spot…

articles.title: Japan to Compensate Oil Importers for High Shipping Costs
articles.description: The Japanese government on Tuesday approved three bills to boost diversification of oil supplies and energy security, including grants to compensate Japan’s oil importers for the high shipping costs to procure supply from alternative sources. The bills will now be introduced for debate at the Japanese Parliament. The legislation is aimed at improving “supply security by diversifying sources of crude oil and other fossil fuels and reducing related risks,” Japan’s Industry ‌Minister…

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Shoots Down Houthi Missiles as Regional Conflict Escalates
articles.description: A day after the two consecutive deadly attacks on the international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen as the Saudi-Houthi standoff escalates and threatens to spill over into further attacks on energy infrastructure. “Two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Khamis Mushait were intercepted and destroyed,” the Saudi Press Agency quoted Major General Turki Al-Malki, official Spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore…

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Plans Massive Expansion of Oil Pipeline to Bypass Hormuz
articles.description: Saudi Arabia plans to raise the capacity of its East-West onshore oil pipeline that helps it bypass the Strait of Hormuz to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) within two to three years, Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said at the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh. The pipeline, which returned to service after a two-week suspension following drone attacks in September, currently carries about 5.8 million bpd, the minister said last week. articles.title: Shell Slams Australia's Plan to Force LNG Producers to Supply Domestic Market
articles.description: Shell has spoken out against a plan by the Australian government to ensure domestic gas supply by mandating LNG producers to reserve certain volumes of their output for domestic use. “Fundamentally, it's a sledgehammer to crack a nut. And it is an extraordinarily heavy-handed intervention into a market that is actually working well,” Shell Australia’s chairwoman, Cecile Wake, said at an industry event in Australia, as quoted by Reuters. articles.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Saudi Arabia Pledges to Keep Exports Flowing
articles.description: Crude oil prices, which topped $106 per barrel yesterday, have eased today, as traders process the latest Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the related risk to energy supply, while also waiting to see if the Russian diesel deal would affect end prices. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $105.43 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $92.60 per barrel, both slightly down from Monday’s close but higher than last week. articles.description: Japanese Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa called for stronger cooperation between oil-producing and consuming countries as well as greater oil stockpiling and infrastructure development in Asia.
